[[1012.12]] 213. Allgemeine Charactere nach Marshall und Becher [1677 bis 1679 (?)]

[[1012.13]] [1677 bis 1679 (?)]

[[1012.18]] That a person of parts, educated only to read and write the Language of the Nation

[[1012.19]] wherein he was born, may in an hours time be taught to set down any matter, secret or

[[1012.20]] other, in another language as Latine, Greek, French etc. and the Latine or other Language

[[1012.21]] to be true and the sense good and continued. ... it may be done many several wayes. ...

[[1012.22]] I have seen the whole Model and Systeme of it in several Languages besides our own,

[[1012.23]] and but that it would make my letter of too great a Bulk should here with have sent you a

[[1012.24]] transcript of one of them.

[[1012.25]] William Marshall Dr. of Physick in London in the first answer of his book intituled:

[[1012.26]] Answers upon several heads in philosophy, London 1670. 8^#'o. pag. 14. Habeo librum.

[[1013.1]] Putem huic scopo inservire etiam posse Becheri Characterem universalem, in quo

[[1013.2]] promittit unius diei informatione ita scribere aliquem docere, ut ab unoquoque in sua

[[1013.3]] lingua intelligatur; adhibitis scilicet Lexicis qui numeros (pro characteribus universalibus

[[1013.4]] hic sumtos) in quaque lingua interpretantur. Eadem autem opera praestare potuisset, quod

[[1013.5]] erat adhuc mirabilius, ut quis posset in qualibet ipsa lingua ignota scribere; modo Lexicon

[[1013.6]] quale opus est, cum paucis quibusdam praeceptis necessariis dentur. Quae ut dixi intra

[[1013.7]] diei spatium disci possunt.
